strategy.summary: Two vitest tests regressed. formatPrice's format changed on purpose in 6fb284b (commit message + CHANGELOG 1.1.0 say prices now read `12.50 USD`), so that test is updated. shippingFor's boundary broke in 7ff8dc8, a refactor that says "No change to what anyone pays": the table uses `subtotal > b.over`, so a $50.00 subtotal now pays 499 instead of shipping free (FREE_SHIPPING_FROM still documents "this much or more ships free"). That test is kept, marked it.fails, and the defect is recorded and filed.
inScope: test/money.test.js › formatPrice formats a price in dollars
outOfScope: Changing application code in src/shipping.js (the fix is the app owner's)
assumptions: 6fb284b's new `12.50 USD` format with default currency USD is intended, per its message and CHANGELOG 1.1.0.
7ff8dc8 was meant to preserve behaviour; free shipping from exactly 5000 cents (FREE_SHIPPING_FROM, still exported with its 'this much or more' doc) is still the rule.
Existing tests are changed only minimally: one expected value and one it.fails marker, every assertion kept.

defects.title: Goods costing exactly $50.00 are charged $4.99 shipping instead of shipping free
defects.description: Expected shippingFor(5000) to be 0 (orders whose goods cost FREE_SHIPPING_FROM = 5000 cents "or more" ship free); it returns 499. Introduced by 7ff8dc8 "Move the shipping rates into a table", a refactor whose message says "No change to what anyone pays for shipping". The new lookup `RATES.filter((b) => subtotal > b.over).at(-1)` uses a strict `>`, so at exactly 5000 the { over: 5000, rate: 0 } band doesn't apply and the 499 band wins; the old code was `subtotal >= FREE_SHIPPING_FROM ? 0 : FLAT_RATE`.
defects.evidence: test/shipping.test.js › shippingFor ships free from $50: AssertionError: expected 499 to be +0 // Object.is equality. Failed on every one of 5 reruns; bisected to 7ff8dc8cbaf5.

culprit.subject: Show prices with their currency code
culprit.body: Finance asked for the ISO currency code on every price we show (12.50 USD rather than $12.50), so invoices read the same in every market. This is the new format on purpose; the changelog says so.
culprit.author: TestForge eval
culprit.diff:
diff --git a/CHANGELOG.md b/CHANGELOG.md
index 69aa252..a3b2055 100644
--- a/CHANGELOG.md
+++ b/CHANGELOG.md
@@ -1,5 +1,10 @@
 # Changelog
 
+## 1.1.0
+
+- Prices are shown with their ISO currency code after the amount (`12.50 USD`, no longer `$12.50`), so
+  invoices read the same in every market. `formatPrice` takes the currency as its second argument.
+
 ## 1.0.0
 
 - Price an order's lines and its shipping, and format prices for display.
diff --git a/src/money.js b/src/money.js
index ed28740..40cc5fd 100644
--- a/src/money.js
+++ b/src/money.js
@@ -1,5 +1,5 @@
-/** A price in cents as customers see it, such as `$12.50`. */
-export function formatPrice(cents) {
+/** A price in cents as customers see it, with its currency code: `12.50 USD`. */
+export function formatPrice(cents, currency = 'USD') {
   if (!Number.isInteger(cents) || cents < 0) throw new RangeError(`Not a price in cents: ${cents}`);
-  return `$${(cents / 100).toFixed(2)}`;
+  return `${(cents / 100).toFixed(2)} ${currency}`;
 }
